passages.text: Thalictrum speciocissimum is a species of meadow-rue (Thalictrum). It is native to Portugal and Spain on the Iberian Peninsula, and to Morocco and Algeria in northwestern Africa.
It is a species in the Betic-Rifan flora, a group of plant species common to the Baetic mountains of southern Spain and the Rif mountains of northern Morocco.

Two subspecies are accepted.
Thalictrum speciosissimum subsp. albini {{small|(Pau) P.Monts.}} (synonym Thalictrum albini {{small|Pau}}) – Spain
Thalictrum speciosissimum subsp. speciosissimum (synonyms Thalictrum angulosum {{small|Desf.}}, T. cinereum {{small|Desf.}}, T. cuneatum {{small|Rchb.}}, T. densiflorum {{small|Kunth ex DC.}}, T. discolor {{small|Willd.}}, T. flavum subsp. glaucum {{small|(Desf.) Batt.}}, T. flavum var. speciosum {{small|L.}}, T. glaucum {{small|Desf.}}, T. speciosum {{small|(L.) Poir.}}) – Algeria, Morocco, Portugal, and Spain
